semantic_correction.stem: A client preparing for major elective surgery is referred to a prehabilitation program. Which plan best reflects the purpose of prehabilitation?

options.A: Begin individualized exercise and nutrition support before surgery, with education or psychological support added when appropriate.
options.B: Wait until postoperative functional decline occurs before starting exercise, nutrition, or recovery-focused support.
options.C: Avoid physical activity before surgery so functional reserve is conserved for the postoperative recovery period.
options.D: Use prehabilitation instead of routine perioperative and postoperative rehabilitation because the programs serve the same purpose.

semantic_correction.rationale: The American College of Surgeons defines prehabilitation as improving a patient's functional capability before a surgical procedure so the patient is better able to withstand postoperative inactivity and functional decline. Current ACS materials describe prehabilitation programs as care provided before surgery that can include structured exercise, nutrition optimization, psychological support, and education. A 2026 ACS review also found that exercise- and nutrition-based prehabilitation programs can improve postoperative outcomes. Prehabilitation therefore begins before surgery and complements rather than replaces perioperative and postoperative care.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Identify prehabilitation as proactive preoperative optimization of functional capacity using interventions such as exercise, nutrition, education, and psychological support.
semantic_correction.source_document_title: Prehabilitation; Optimizing Exercise, Nutrition Before Surgery Boosts Patient Outcomes; Exercise-, Nutrition-Based Prehabilitation Programs Show Promise in Enhancing Recovery
semantic_correction.source_version_date: ACS Prehabilitation page current in 2026; ACS evidence summaries published April 29 and May 5, 2026; accessed August 21, 2026
semantic_correction.source_locator: Prehabilitation — defined as improving functional capability before surgery so the patient can withstand postoperative inactivity and decline. April 29, 2026 ACS review — prehabilitation is care before surgery to improve health and may include exercise, nutrition, psychological support, and education. May 5, 2026 ACS Brief — exercise- and nutrition-based programs are promising strategies for enhancing surgical recovery
semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: ACS describes prehabilitation as preoperative optimization of functional capability and health, commonly using exercise and nutrition and sometimes psychological support and education, to improve readiness for surgery and recovery.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: removed 'all/only' distractor cueing, shortened the uniquely long correct answer, and anchored the item to current ACS evidence that prehabilitation is proactive care before surgery centered on functional and nutritional optimization with additional support as appropriate.

audit_findings_append.source_locator: ACS Prehabilitation page plus April–May 2026 evidence summaries
audit_findings_append.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — preoperative health optimization
audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item accurately tests prehabilitation as preoperative optimization rather than postoperative rescue, inactivity, or a substitute for routine perioperative care.

option_audit.A: Correct. It reflects ACS descriptions of prehabilitation as preoperative exercise/nutrition optimization with other supportive components as appropriate.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Prehabilitation occurs before surgery rather than waiting for postoperative decline.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Exercise is a core prehabilitation component and is intended to improve functional reserve, not conserve it through inactivity.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Prehabilitation complements rather than replaces routine perioperative and postoperative care.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone reflects the timing, purpose, and components of current ACS prehabilitation guidance.
cueing_check: All four options are prehabilitation plans of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
